identity.title: The SCUBA-2 Cosmology Legacy Survey: ALMA Resolves the Bright-end of the Sub-millimeter Number Counts

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present high-resolution 870 $\mu$m ALMA continuum maps of 30 bright sub-millimeter sources in the UKIDSS UDS field.

targets.name: 30 SCUBA-2 S2CLS sources in the UKIDSS UDS field (e.g. UDS156, UDS286)

evidence.quote: From these earlier observations we selected 31 sources detected at $>$ 4 $\sigma$, and hence having observed 850–$\mu$m flux densities of $>$ 8mJy.
From these earlier observations we selected 31 sources detected at $>$ 4 $\sigma$, and hence having observed 850–$\mu$m flux densities of $>$ 8mJy.

question.value: How often are bright SCUBA-2 850 um sources blends of multiple SMGs, and what are the intrinsic bright-end number counts and the origin of the multiplicity?

evidence.quote: We use the data to measure the multiplicity in the single-dish population, probe the bright–end of the number counts and investigate the number density of secondary SMGs.
as part of the Cycle-1 project 2012.1.00090.S
We obtained ALMA 870 $\mu$m (Band 7) continuum imaging of all 30 targets from our sample on 2013 November 1

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: single continuum setup, four basebands of 128 dual-polarization channels

evidence.quote: We used a “single continuum” correlator setup with four basebands of 128 dual-polarization channels each.
All targets were observed using 7.5-GHz of bandwidth centered at 344 GHz (870 $\mu$m)
The observations were conducted using 26 12–m antennae with a range of baselines from 20 to 1250 m, and a median baseline of 200 m.
a range of baselines from 20 to 1250 m, and a median baseline of 200 m
The array configuration yields a synthesized beam of 0.35$''$ $\times$ 0.25$''$ using Briggs weighting (robust parameter = 0.5)
The final maps have a range of 1–$\sigma_{870}$ depths from 0.19–0.24 mJy beam$^{-1}$ (median $\sigma_{870} =$ 0.21 mJy beam$^{-1}$).
In total each target was observed five times (total integration time of 150 s)
on 2013 November 1, as part of the Cycle-1 project 2012.1.00090.S

provided.value: 850 um maps used to select the 30 targets and for flux comparison

evidence.quote: The sub-mm sources in this paper were selected from observations taken as part of the S2CLS programme at the JCMT.

what.value: ALESS/LESS ALMA number counts combined with this sample for double power-law fit

evidence.quote: We now combine our sample with the ALESS survey (cite: Karim13), with the aim of providing a single parameterization of the intrinsic sub-mm number counts

what.value: Faint serendipitous ALMA counts at 1.2 and 1.3 mm converted to 870 um

evidence.quote: we also include two studies that have used serendipitous detections of sources in deep targeted ALMA observations to measure the number counts of faint SMGs at 1.2 and 1.3 mm

what.value: Composite ALESS SMG SED at z=2.5 for flux conversion; S870-LFIR relation

evidence.quote: We convert these counts to 870 $\mu$m using the composite SMG spectral energy distribution (SED) from the ALESS survey (see (cite: Swinbank13)), redshifted to $z$ = 2.5
To determine the magnitude of this effect we use a simulation of single-dish observations of SMGs, presented by (cite: Cowley15).

pipeline_or_manual.value: CASA used for calibration and imaging; manual vs pipeline not stated

evidence.quote: The calibration and imaging of our science targets, and calibrators, was performed using the Common Astronomy Software Application (casa version 4.2.1).
We repeated the data reduction using the most recent version of casa (4.2.2) and found it had no effect on our final maps or source catalog.
The absolute flux scale for each measurement set was derived from observations of J 0238+166

flux_scale_uncertainty.value: calibrator varies up to 10% day to day

evidence.quote: the ALMA calibrator archive shows that this source has day–to–day variations of up to 10 $\%$
To image each target we first Fourier transform the $uv$–data to create a “dirty” map, using Briggs weighting (robust parameter = 0.5).
using Briggs weighting (robust parameter = 0.5)

uv_taper.value: natural weighting plus 0.6'' Gaussian taper for detection maps

evidence.quote: we repeated the imaging process using natural weighting, and applied a 0.6$''$ Gaussian taper in the $uv$–plane
Both the “detection” and higher resolution maps have a size of 36$''$ $\times$ 36$''$, and a pixel scale of 0.04$''$.
Both the “detection” and higher resolution maps have a size of 36$''$ $\times$ 36$''$

masking.value: clean to 3 sigma; if >5 sigma source, tight clean box and clean to 1.5 sigma

evidence.quote: If a source is detected at $>5$ $\sigma$ then we repeat the cleaning process but place a tight clean box around each $>5$ $\sigma$ source and clean the dirty map to $1.5$ $\sigma$.
The fluxes measured in both sets of maps are primary–beam corrected using the model of the primary beam response output by casa.
These low–resolution “detection” maps have a median rms of $\sigma_{870} =$ 0.26 mJy beam$^{-1}$ and a median synthesized beam of 0.8 $'' \times$ 0.65$''$.
median $\sigma_{870} =$ 0.21 mJy beam$^{-1}$

findings_qualitative.value: Counts decline strongly at the bright end with no sharp cut-off.

evidence.quote: We detect bright SMGs in our survey and do not find evidence for a sharp cut–off in the counts.

claims.finding: Multiplicity is common and boosts single-dish counts by 20% at >7.5 mJy and 60% at >12 mJy

evidence.quote: In 61$^{+19}_{-15}$ $\%$  of the ALMA maps the single-dish source comprises a blend of $\ge$ 2 SMGs

evidence.quote: we do find that number counts decline strongly towards the bright-end with a distinct break
